Sample Missing-Value Locations with Constraints

Source: R/tune_imp.R
sample_na_loc.Rd

Draws matrix positions for NA injection. The positions respect row and column limits on missing values and skip constant columns.

Usage

sample_na_loc(
  obj,
  n_cols = NULL,
  n_rows = 2L,
  num_na = NULL,
  n_reps = 1L,
  rowmax = 0.9,
  colmax = 0.9,
  na_col_subset = NULL,
  max_attempts = 100
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix.

n_cols

Integer or NULL. Number of columns that receive missing values.

n_rows

Integer. Minimum number of missing values per selected column.

num_na

Integer or NULL. Total number of missing values per repetition. When given, n_cols is ignored and the values are spread as evenly as possible over num_na %/% n_rows columns.

n_reps

Integer. Number of independent repetitions.

rowmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Maximum proportion of missing values per row after injection.

colmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Maximum proportion of missing values per column after injection.

na_col_subset

Optional character or integer vector. The columns that can receive missing values, by name or by number.

max_attempts

Integer. Maximum number of sampling attempts per repetition before an error.

Value

A list of length n_reps. Each element is a two-column integer matrix, with columns row and col, of the sampled NA locations.

Details

sample_na_loc() places the NA locations by a greedy random search. Every result meets these limits:

  • The proportion of missing values in each row and column, existing ones included, stays at or under rowmax and colmax.

  • Every selected column keeps at least two distinct observed values.

  • A column with a variance below .Machine$double.eps counts as constant and is never selected. pca_imp() uses the same threshold to leave a column out of its fit.

A column that cannot take n_rows missing values under these limits is skipped without an error.

When both n_cols and num_na are NULL, num_na defaults to 5% of the cells of obj, with a maximum of 500. The default never asks for more columns than the number that can take n_rows missing values.

See also

  • tune_imp(), which takes the result as na_loc.

  • mipca_tune(), which takes a result with n_reps = 1 as na_loc.

Examples

set.seed(123)
mat <- matrix(runif(100), nrow = 10)

# Sample 5 missing values across 5 columns
locs <- sample_na_loc(mat, n_cols = 5, n_rows = 1)
locs
#> [[1]]
#>      row col
#> [1,]   8   6
#> [2,]   5   1
#> [3,]   3   2
#> [4,]   2   4
#> [5,]   4   8
#> 

# Inject the missing values from the first repetition
mat[locs[[1]]] <- NA
mat
